AssessmentRecommendations.Title: ORDER BY specifies integer ordinal
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: This rule checks stored procedures, functions, views and triggers for use of ORDER BY clause specifying ordinal column numbers as sort columns. A sort column can be specified as a nonnegative integer representing the position of the name or alias in the select list, but this is not recommended. An integer cannot be specified when the order_by_expression appears in a ranking function. A sort column can include an expression, but when the database is in SQL 90 compatibility mode or higher, the expression cannot resolve to a constant.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation: Specify the sort column as a name or column alias rather than hard coding the ordinal.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
Bad habits to kick : ORDER BY ordinal (https://aka.ms/order-by-integer)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: CLR assemblies marked as SAFE or EXTERNAL_ACCESS are considered UNSAFE
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: CLR Strict Security mode is introduced in SQL Server 2017. This mode is enabled by default and introduces breaking changes for databases containing user-defined CLR assemblies marked either SAFE or EXTERNAL_ACCESS.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
When CLR Strict Security is enabled, attempting to create an unsigned assembly will cause an error. Use the following steps to create a signed assembly:

  1. Create a key pair file. For more information, see How to: Create a Public-Private Key Pair.
  2. Compile the module and sign it using the key file. For more information, see How to: Sign an Assembly with a Strong Name.

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)
